title: Rudolf/Harvard Blaschka receiving reconstruction — state, authority and labor model
research_question: What operations, actors and authority changes convert a Blaschka transport assemblage into a stable museum/exhibition object after arrival?
current_thesis: Unpacking was a receiving-side craft of serial reconstruction, not the simple inverse of packing. The transport assemblage had to be legally opened, materially dismantled, inspected, sometimes repaired, detached from temporary supports, remounted, labelled and stabilized by actors whose authorities and skills were distributed across patronage, customs, curatorship and paid technical work.

authority_transitions.transition: tissue-supported fragile model → safely released model

direct_functions: personal unpacking according to Harvard finding aid

non_claims: no evidence for delicate inner-model unpacking beyond source description
do not describe as model handler without evidence
inspection authority is not equivalent to delicate handling skill
do not back-project 1930s title to all earlier years

public_demonstration_events.event: Goodale demonstrates packing and three recent models are unpacked before Boston Society of Natural History audience
Customs-supervised new importation unpacking treated as 'a matter of considerable interest'; President Eliot and Mrs. Eliot invited; Goodale later shows packing/unpacking in Ware's presence

material_risk_rules.risk: rings/jackets/shawls/coats catch on fragile model parts
models strongly bound to framed transport plates
material_risk_rules.mitigation: skilled loosening, time and patience before remounting
repair, remount, relabel and stress-test display

already_known_ground: museum collections depend on backstage material labor and care
preparators/technicians have histories in nineteenth-century natural-history museums
modern registrar/collections-management functions include logistics, packing, handling and installation
do_not_claim: that Blaschka/Harvard invented museum technical labor
that Mary Ware was a proto-registrar
that Waugh/Bierweiler form a simple linear professionalization narrative
historiographical_calibration.stronger_specific_contribution: The Blaschka correspondence allows receiving work to be reconstructed transaction by transaction as a choreography of differentiated authority and skill around an exceptionally fragile object. It also shows this work being publicly demonstrated, explicitly paid, technically codified and trusted by the maker across decades.

map_implication.decision: do not add more geographic lines yet
map_implication.recommended_projection: use the full-width map for person/packet routes; use the lower evidence strip for a state timeline showing transport assemblage → customs-openable → unpacked → remounted → installed → repaired/restabilized
map_implication.reason: settlement and unpacking events are state/authority transitions, often within one geographic node, and drawing them as routes would confuse movement with reconstruction

next_questions: Can John Waugh's payment receipt be tied to a precise dollar amount and employment identity?
